metadata.title: Nesh — Web Push, made simple
metadata.description: A lightweight Web Push SaaS for Next.js / React projects. The hosted alternative to OneSignal — sign up, drop the SDK in, start sending.

samples.title: Web Push, delivered
samples.body: The notification you sent 2 minutes ago was just delivered.

features.title: The features you need to send. Nothing else.
features.subtitle: No segmentation. No journeys. No A/B tests. Just reliable Web Push.

send.title: Send in seconds
send.body: Compose in the dashboard or POST to a Bearer-auth endpoint. Synchronous response includes per-subscriber delivery counts.

rest.title: REST API
rest.body: One endpoint per project. Use it from any backend, CI, or curl. No SDK required on the server.

userIds.title: External user IDs
userIds.body: Tag subscriptions with your own user IDs and target sends by user from the dashboard or REST.

webhooks.title: Signed webhooks
webhooks.body: HMAC-SHA256 signatures, exponential-backoff retry, per-event filtering. Delivery log + replay UI included.

analytics.title: Built-in analytics
analytics.body: Shown / clicked beacons fire from the SDK service worker — no extra tools to wire up.

openSource.title: Open source
openSource.body: MIT licensed end-to-end. Read the code, fork it, audit the storage. Self-hosting guide included.

comparison.title: Web Push only. Nothing else.
comparison.subtitle: We skip the marketing-suite features on purpose. In return you get readable code, ownership of your data, and no vendor lock-in.

dashboardPreview.title: A dashboard that fits on one screen
dashboardPreview.subtitle: No nested menus to learn. Every project's status at a glance.
dashboardPreview.imageAlt: Nesh dashboard showing a project with subscriber count, monthly sends, and notification history

howItWorks.title: From signup to first send
howItWorks.subtitle: Three steps, one code snippet.
howItWorks.step1Body: Sign up and create a project. We generate VAPID keys and an API key for you.
howItWorks.step2Body: Install @piro0919/next-push and pass apiBase + publicKey from the SDK setup screen.
howItWorks.step3Body: Compose in the dashboard, schedule it, or POST to the REST endpoint.

pricing.title: Free for the entire early access period
pricing.subtitle: Nesh is a self-funded side project — no VC, no "surprise paywall" exit. Long-term pricing will be announced in advance once it's decided.

items.sends: 10,000 sends per project per UTC month

free.a: Yes, free during early access — within the caps shown above. Long-term pricing isn't decided yet (Nesh is a side project run by one developer, not a VC-backed startup).

vsOneSignal.a: OneSignal is great if you need segmentation, A/B tests, journeys. Nesh is for people who find that overkill and want a tiny dashboard with the essentials — and an open codebase.

selfHost.a: Yes — the code is MIT and runs on any Postgres + Vercel-compatible host. See the <selfHost>self-hosting guide</selfHost> for the full setup.

native.a: Web Push only for now. Web Push works on iOS Safari (16.4+) when installed as a PWA.

privacy.a: Subscriptions, notification metadata, and shown/clicked counts. No 3rd-party trackers. VAPID private keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest.

finalCta.title: Ship Web Push this afternoon
finalCta.subtitle: No setup call. No credit card. No five-page onboarding.

sdk.title: SDK reference
sdk.intro: Returns subscription helpers and reactive state.

rows.apiBase: Full URL of the project's API base. Use the value shown in the SDK setup card.
rows.userId: Optional — your application user id. Lets the dashboard / REST API target sends to specific users.
rows.swScope: Override the SW registration scope (e.g. "/" when serving from a sub-path).

subscribe.title: Subscribe
subscribe.body: Called by the SDK after the browser issues a push subscription. CORS-enabled, no auth.
subscribe.note: Rate limited 60 / minute per IP × project × action. The endpoint also enforces the free-tier subscriber cap on new endpoints (existing endpoints can always update).

send.title: Send notification
send.body: Server-to-server. Use the <bearer></bearer> token from the project's API key card (format <key></key>). Synchronous — the response includes delivery counts.
send.note: Subject to the monthly send cap (10,000 / project / UTC month on the free tier). Returns when reached.

track.title: Track event (SDK / SW)
track.body: Service Workers POST shown / clicked beacons here automatically when the SDK is v0.6+. You shouldn't normally call this from your code.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.intro1: Configure one or more webhook URLs on the project page. Every enabled webhook receives a JSON <post></post> signed with <hmac></hmac> for each event. Failed deliveries (5xx / 408 / 429 / network errors) are retried with exponential backoff (30s → 2m → 10m → 1h, 5 attempts max). The <attempt></attempt> header counts the attempt number when retried.
webhooks.intro2: Each webhook can be filtered to a subset of event types from the project page. The default (all checkboxes selected) subscribes the webhook to every event.

events.title: Events
events.notificationSent: After a notification finishes sending (dashboard / REST / cron).
events.subscriptionCreated: A brand-new endpoint subscribed (re-subscribes do not refire).
events.subscriptionRemoved: A subscription was removed — by the client (DELETE) or because the push service returned 404/410.

webhooks.removedReason: <client></client> means the SDK / dashboard called DELETE; <expired></expired> means the push service returned 404/410 during a send and Nesh dropped the dead subscription automatically.

verify.title: Verifying the signature (Node.js)
verify.note: Always compare bodies as raw bytes (read the request body before parsing JSON). Webhook delivery has a 5-second timeout; non-2xx responses are recorded as the last delivery error and shown on the dashboard.

limits.title: Free-tier limits

rows.sends: Sends per project per UTC month

limits.note: Hard caps return <c403></c403> (subscribers) or <c429></c429> (sends). <faq>More on the FAQ</faq>.

selfHost.title: Self-hosting
selfHost.intro: Nesh is MIT-licensed and runs on any Node-compatible host with a Postgres database. The reference deploy targets Vercel + Supabase, but neither is required.

reqs.title: Requirements
reqs.node: Node.js 20+ (the Vercel build image works as-is).
reqs.pg: Postgres 15+ — Supabase, Neon, RDS, or self-hosted all work.
reqs.host: Any Node-compatible host that runs the Next.js build output (Vercel, Cloudflare, Fly.io, a VM, Docker).
reqs.https: HTTPS on the production origin — browsers refuse to register Service Workers over plain HTTP.

step1.title: 1. Clone and install
step1.body: Clone the repository and install dependencies.

step2.title: 2. Provision Postgres + apply migrations
step2.bodyLead: All schema is in . If you're using Supabase, the project ships with the CLI — start the local stack with
step2.bodyCli: and apply the same migrations to your remote project. For non-Supabase Postgres, run the SQL files in in filename order.
step2.rls: Row-Level Security is enabled on every table. The dashboard talks to Postgres as the signed-in user via Supabase auth; server routes that bypass RLS (cron, REST send) use the service role key.

env.supabaseUrl: Postgres URL exposed by Supabase (or any PostgREST endpoint).
env.supabaseAnon: Anonymous (publishable) key — safe to expose to the browser.
env.supabaseService: Service-role key — server-only, bypasses RLS. Treat like a database password.
env.siteUrl: Public origin of your Nesh deployment. Used to build the apiBase shown to SDK users and the public event tracking URL.
env.cronSecret: Shared secret the cron job uses to authenticate. Any sufficiently random string.
env.vapidKeyEnc: 32-byte AES-256-GCM key for encrypting per-project VAPID private keys at rest. Generate with the command below — losing this key means losing access to every existing project's VAPID identity.
env.adminUserIds: Optional. Comma-separated list of Supabase user UUIDs that can access the /admin dashboard.

step4.title: 4. Deploy
step4.vercelLead: Vercel: connect the repo, set the env vars from step 3, and deploy. The included wires up the cron schedule automatically.
step4.noteCron: On non-Vercel hosts you'll need to schedule yourself — see step 5.

step5.title: 5. Schedule the cron worker
step5.body: The cron worker dispatches scheduled notifications, retries failed webhook deliveries, and prunes rate-limit rows. It should run roughly every minute. Authenticate it with the as a Bearer token.
step5.vercel: On Vercel: the bundled already declares this schedule.
step5.manual: Outside Vercel: any scheduler will do — GitHub Actions, fly.io machines, cron + curl, Kubernetes CronJob. Example crontab:

step6.title: 6. First user and admin
step6.body: Sign up via the UI to create your account. Look up your user UUID in Supabase Studio (or via SQL) and add it to to unlock the /admin dashboard.

notes.title: Operational notes
notes.encKey: must not change after projects exist. Back it up alongside your database. Rotation requires re-encrypting every projects.vapid_private_key.
notes.scaling: Web Push fan-out runs serially per project inside the send route (max ~5000 subs per project on the bundled tier). If you raise that ceiling, consider moving the fan-out to a queue.
notes.tracking: Event tracking (shown / clicked) hits a public endpoint by design — beacons send no credentials. Rate limited per IP.
notes.logs: Server errors are persisted to and surfaced on /admin. Useful when debugging a deploy.
